newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-ARGENTINE LEAGUE STRIKE STILL LOOMS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARGENTINE LEAGUE STRIKE STILL LOOMS.

text.p: Talks to head off a strike by Argentina's professional soccer players before Sunday's league matches adjourned after a second day without agreement on Thursday.
The concilliation talks between the Argentine Football Association (AFA) and the players' union at the Labour Ministry will resume on Friday.
Players voted on Tuesday to strike until troubled first division side Deportivo Espanol agreed to allow six players whose contracts expired on June 30 to move to other sides.
The dispute was complicated when a judge ruled that the players counted as assets of the heavily-indebted club, and so cannot leave until all creditors have been paid.
While talks dragged on, the AFA issued a statement on Thursday backing the players' union against the club.

"The (six Deportivo Espanol) players cannot have their right to work complicated by administrative or legal matters, which have nothing to do with them and the AFA will take action to demand their contractual freedom," the AFA said.
